steps.content: From behind the slightly open door comes the sound of dragging footsteps. Shrooma pushes the door open and shuffles in with her rubber clogs, standing nonchalantly in front of you.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Why did you send for me suddenly? I thought you've blacklisted me or something!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Or is ignoring me not enough? You must get rid of me, huh? Am I on your to-be-executed list?
She talks with bubble gum in her mouth, occasionally blowing a pink bubble, but not skillful enough to make it last.
You've already heard from Nightingale about her recent behavior, but witnessing it with your own eyes still amuses you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As far as I know, the Bureau doesn't have such a list.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But I'm glad to see you so active, Shrooma. It seems your life has become much more eventful in just a few days?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: How can I resist? Everyone here is so having the gift of the gab. I just love it!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Besides, I've even got the wonderful Chief to care about me, haven't I? I'm simply overwhelmed with surprise!
She has an indifferent, cheeky grin on her face, as if waiting for you to look disgusted and scold her. But you simply smile gently.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, I'm the one who should be surprised. Why are you suddenly so candid in front of me? Have you given up on acting like a good kid?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What happened to "I did nothing wrong. You will see that very soon"?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Hey, you're not being fair. Haven't we done the tree hole-shouting thing together already? Why are you still playing dumb with me?
She points at the folder on the desk with her chin, her tone increasing precocious.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You've spent days investigating before coming to me. You must have all the evidence to keep me trapped for ten... No, for a lifetime.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: So why would I keep pretending? I've got nothing to lose anyway!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't think you've done anything deserving of lifelong detention in the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Huh? Is it fun to bait me? Or you wanna force me to confess it myself?
The look in her eyes changes. You don't want to be seen as an adult with a cruel sense of humor. You drop the jest and get straight to the point.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sorry, but I really don't think you're capable of making such a grave mistake.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If I have to guess... Perhaps you're talking about your twin sister?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...So you did find out.
The indifferent smile is wiped from Shrooma's face. Under her gaze, you slowly open the folder, revealing an old hospital report.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That day, I happened to overhear Joshua mentioning your mother and... your sister.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But according to our records, you're an only child.
With a pop, the longest-lasting bubble Shrooma has blown finally bursts. The clear sound resembles the unveiling of a secret within a glass dome.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So I visited the hospital where your mother was registered as a maternity patient. With some effort, I finally found her medical records.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The prenatal check-up records were for twins, but the visits had been interrupted inexplicably. In the end, there was only the birth certificate for one girl.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...So what? Anything to prove with this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This proves nothing, indeed. Usually it just means an unsuspicious pregnancy termination or an unfortunate birth accident. But...
You turn to the later pages in the folder and show Shrooma the medical report from when she first joined the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your medical report shows several abnormal values. Comparing them to existing cases, our medical department believes you likely became a Sinner due to maternal infection.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Moreover, we've visited your mother's former neighbors and household employees. They've all confirmed she barely left home during her pregnancy.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Combining the factors... We can probably deduce that your mother came into contact with some Mania contaminant during her pregnancy, right?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: How would I know since I was still in my mother's belly... but I suppose it's something like that!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: But then what? Sounds like I'm still the poor innocent victim here? Chief, you're not telling me you've been moved by an evil monster like me and want to clear my name?
The girl in front of you is like a cat trapped in a box, scraping at the lid with her sharp claws, hoping someone would come and check on her to see whether she's dead or alive.
You look at her, and decide to tear those old scabs from her wounds.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's everything we have evidence for. From now on, whatever I say is just speculation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because of Mania, you're the only twin that survived. Because of Mania, you became a Sinner and your power awakened, which gave you the camouflaging ability.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because she was carrying a baby Sinner in her, your mother only absorbed a trace of Mania and, just like you who was born with the camouflaging ability, she also miraculously survived the contamination.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...Miraculously?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, it was a miracle. Because of this one-in-a-million accident, your reputation-conscious family didn't abandon you both.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yet they hold a natural fear toward Mania, and even more toward those who can overcome Mania. They blame your sister's death on you, and you've always lived under their scrutiny and surveillance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's why Joshua can show his true nature, but not you. You must always be better than anyone else just to be accepted, right?
A moment of silence follows. The air is filled with nothing but the sinking weight of the question you've just posed.
Suddenly, Shrooma raises her hands and starts clapping vigorously.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Amazing! You nailed it! What an armchair detective you are, Chief!

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: You're right about everything! I'm an evil seed tainted by Mania, a nuisance my family must watch over, a villain who hides her identity as a Sinner! Even my own mother is afraid of me!
She seems to have suddenly let go of her fear, agreeing with you with a shrill voice, her palms all red from clapping as if she feels no pain.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Someone like me should never be let out, right? Isn't that enough to keep me locked up in the Bureau my whole life?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shrooma, calm down!
You grab her wrist, interrupting her outburst reluctantly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You said it yourself. You were tainted by Mania. The Bureau has no right to keep a victim locked up for life.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We'll only help you control the Mania and rid yourself of its influence as much as possible, so you can return to normal life.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Victim? What victim? Me?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: That's hilarious. So that's how the Bureau cares for its criminals? Are you some kind of charity?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Oh, shut it please. Even my mother has never covered me up like this!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I know you're not thinking straight as you speak now...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But Shrooma, regarding this matter, your understanding seems to differ from reality.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I have another testimony that's probably more credible.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Since you recognize me, does that mean you already know that Shrooma...

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: Of course. Shrooma is my flesh and blood, after all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you also know about those posts, and that Shrooma often...
A rustle of fabric. Perhaps the lady has taken out a handkerchief. After a while, she takes a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: I know Shrooma has never been happy in this household. And she's probably done some things she shouldn't have at her age.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: But she's not the one at fault. If anyone has made a mistake, it's me. As her mother, I've failed to protect her.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: When I was pregnant with Shrooma, as a result of some conflicts of interest, someone bribed my maid to place something... "unclean" in my room.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: The family wouldn't abandon any of its members, so I didn't die. I was just sent away and kept under close watch.
Her voice trembles slightly, as if the cold from her memories could freeze her blood.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: I knew any abnormal sign in me would mean my murder. The countdown to my death had long begun.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: So I was scared to death. I was scared of becoming a monster, that my children might not be born, that I wouldn't even get to hold them...

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: Oh... I'm sorry. I know I'm not a brave mother. Even now, I still see that unchanging ceiling from those days in my nightmares...

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: At that time, lying on that hospital bed, I couldn't catch even a glimpse of the sun. I could only hold on to my belly and keep praying.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: I prayed that my children would be okay, that they could survive... If not both, then let at least one of them live!

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: Even if she turned out to be a monster! As long as she could disguise herself and live on!

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: Yes, I wanted to survive. Even if my children and I turned into monsters, I still wanted us to live on together... Have you ever met a more selfish mother, Chief?
She lets out an almost inaudible sob. Clearly, this unspeakable secret has not only crushed Shrooma, but deeply hurt her as well.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: I could feel my child trying hard to meet my expectations, struggling to survive. Finally, I met my Shrooma.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: "Gain more nutrients and become strong." "Even if you become a monster, don't let anyone find out." "Hide it. Conceal your nature carefully and live on."...

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: She was just like an angel coming straight out of my prayers! She saved herself, and she saved me! She allowed us both to survive!

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: It was as if... my cowardice, my fear, my selfishness were transmitted through the umbilical cord to my child, changing her...!

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: ...Thank you. You see, it was my selfish expectations that changed her and made her the way she is. That's why she's now under so much pressure.

steps.speaker: Shrooma's Mother
steps.content: But none of this is a burden she should carry. She did nothing wrong. She is just too obedient...
The recording turns into white noise. Shrooma looks dazed, her face blank with disbelief. At this moment, she finally looks like a child.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Her fault? What does this have to do with her? Why should she take all the blame?

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: She's always taught me to "Be patient. Be kind. Be considerate. Be sensible." But I've failed her. It's my fault!
Her gaze goes blank, like she's tracing her mother's frail figure in those repressed memories. You sigh and begin gently.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes. "Be patient. Be kind. Be considerate. Be sensible." ...She must have advised you like this many times, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did you always think that she kept warning and restraining you like the other elders did because she didn't want to accept your true nature?
But in fact...

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: She didn't mean to discipline or restrain me... She was just teaching me what kind of camouflage I must wear in order to survive in the family...

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: I never thought... blessings could come in this form too...
Seeing Shrooma's moist eyes and pursed lips, you grow more determined not to let this story end in tears.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shrooma, as a victim of Mania, both you and your mother were powerless against this contamination.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Those responsible for the loss of that life are the merchant behind the plot, the maid who executed it, and Mania that has harmed countless people, but not you or your mother.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In fact...
You hand Shrooma a research report. It demonstrates with lucid charts the survival rate of mothers and embryos in similar situations. A number infinitely close to 0.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You and your mother created an almost miracle. You didn't overconsume to the point of even devouring her, and she managed to protect a child under Mania.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: ...Is that true? You're not tricking me?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No. In fact, the current laws can't punish you, and you don't have to fear losing everything because of your identity as a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Someone in your family will always love and support you. Your guardian, your mother, she will take responsibility and protect you from the pressure of the family.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just like she protected you at the banquet that day.
Shrooma's slightly confused expression is adorable, making you smile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did you think we gave out leave approval to just any Sinner without the primary guardian's permission?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She withstood the pressure from the whole family and stopped them from investigating your whereabouts. And she let you attend that banquet to dispel the rumors around you in your social circle.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: From now on, she will visit you regularly. She'll cooperate with the Bureau to teach you everything you need to know as you grow up, including how to properly handle your emotions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll also help you control your Mania to prevent emotional outbursts and uncontrollable malice from forming.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shrooma, you are protected and accepted. What you need to do next is learn the knowledge necessary for a Sinner to return to normal life, then continue living your life. That's all.
Her lips tremble. A childish look of grievance finally emerges on her face.

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Is a kid like me worthy of that too...

steps.speaker: Shrooma
steps.content: Someone who... at birth...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A brave child like you who protected your mother at birth is certainly worthy of that.
Shrooma finally lowers her head. Rubbing her eyes, she begins crying loudly like a child who's finally brought back to the side of her parent.
You reach out and ruffle her hair heavily. This time, she doesn't resist.
A tiny hill of documents is piled up on your desk. Nightingale stands by your side. You rub your brow wearily.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Let's call it a day.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: By the way, how's Shrooma doing these days?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She's been back to school for about a week.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What's the situation?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She seems much more cheerful and has made some new friends. However...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She still occasionally posts online. They're mainly complaints about some arrogant classmates.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: But her wording sounds much milder and she doesn't post as often as before.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Hmm, I guess she needs an outlet after all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just let her be. She always comes up with some fancy thoughts. It's cute, isn't it?
